This is actually everything I'd want out of a voat/reddit-esque platform. Decentralized, so that no one country could control the content that gets posted on it (yeah, it be whatever country the "node" lived in, but hey, that's better than being beholden to a single countries moral imperative), and free from censorship at the level of a couple corporate-level individuals.

Biggest barrier here will be the start, due to the monetized nature of the project. Hopefully that isn't a large an obstacle as I fear it will be.

I've often wondered if it could be done on a general level. Like a decentralized service that can be used to make video sharing easier like a decentralized youtube. Or a decentralized imgur. To take a concept of volunteer computing (think of something like seti@home), but with a global web interface on it for the services we use now. It'd be like a decentralized OS, but the apps would be similar to the popular sites we use today.

But I'll admit the idea seems a bit far-fetched and I've never done much to flesh it out. I have no idea how you'd protect against the threat of a brigade of rogue nodes attempting to subvert the system.. Asymmetrically-privileged nodes are just a lighter shade of centralization (some group of people have to own the super nodes). Nor am I convinced that users would go for literally buying into a system just to earn trust such as is proposed by a TrustDavis model.
